findings.source_quote: τίνι ἔτι τοῦτό τις δοῦναι δύναται ἢ καὶ τὸ γενέσθαι δύνασθαι;
findings.english_quote: to whom else can anyone grant this, or even grant that it is capable of coming into being?
findings.issue: The draft interprets the second object as justice itself being capable of coming into existence. A material alternative keeps τίνι governing both grants: to whom can one grant being just, or even the ability to become just? On that reading, the recipient is the implicit subject of the infinitives, and 'just' is understood from the preceding τὸ δικαίῳ εἶναι. The note supplies another paraphrase of the abstract-emergence reading, but neither preserves this recipient/capacity alternative nor explains the preference for justice as the implicit subject. This is an interpretive-disclosure problem, not source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare the source-transparent candidate 'to whom else can anyone grant this—or even the ability to become just?' If adopting it, explain that 'just' is contextually understood, not separately printed. If retaining the abstract-emergence reading, preserve the recipient/capacity alternative and explain the grammatical and contextual grounds for the chosen subject. Submit the resulting text and notes for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: (ὁ μὲν γὰρ παρὼν κόσμος πρόσκαιρος, ὁ δὲ ἐσόμενος ἀΐδιος.)
findings.english_quote: (For the present world is temporary, but the coming age is eternal.)
findings.issue: The second member prints no noun: ὁ δὲ ἐσόμενος means 'but the coming [one].' Supplying 'age' is contextually defensible from the preceding κόσμον, αἰῶνα, but the immediate balanced construction also naturally supplies κόσμος, yielding 'the world to come.' The draft silently selects 'age' and does not disclose or explain this material referent choice. Because the surrounding passage explicitly distinguishes and alternates κόσμος and αἰών, the source-transparent 'world' candidate requires comparison.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare '(For the present world is temporary, but the world to come is eternal.)' Alternatively, preserve the ellipsis with 'but the one to come is eternal.' Add a note identifying the unexpressed second noun, the viable κόσμος/αἰών referents, and the contextual reason for the selected rendering. Any revised wording and notes require fresh review.
